targetWords.definition: To accelerate means to increase in speed.
targetWords.example: When he stepped on the gas pedal, the motorcycle accelerated.

targetWords.definition: If you do something anew, you do it again and in a different way.
targetWords.example: Though he had failed his driving test, he decided to try it anew. defect [difekt] n.

targetWords.definition: —* All these bottles have a defect and must be sent back to the warehouse.
targetWords.example: All these bottles have a defect and must be sent back to the warehouse.

targetWords.definition: If something is dreary, then it is dull, dark, and lifeless.
targetWords.example: After the fire, this section o f forest is rather dreary.

targetWords.definition: To duplicate something means to copy it.
targetWords.example: She duplicated her friend's movements like she was in front o f a mirror.

targetWords.definition: If something is electromagnetic, it is related to electricity and magnetic fields.
targetWords.example: Different colors o f lig h t come from different levels o f electromagnetic energy.

targetWords.definition: An electron is a particle in all atoms that has a negative electric charge.
targetWords.example: The number o f electrons in an atom determines the substance the atoms make.

targetWords.definition: To glide means to fly on extended wings with little or no effort.
targetWords.example: When the wind is blowing, birds can glide easily through the sky.

targetWords.definition: If someone is ingenious, then they are very smart.
targetWords.example: Charles was the only person ingenious enough to repair the plane's engines.

targetWords.definition: An innovation is a product or an idea that is new or very original.
targetWords.example: Mrs. Johnson made a great innovation to the company's business plan. ■1

targetWords.definition: If something or someone is innovative, they can think in creative ways.
targetWords.example: Since Peter was so innovative, he was chosen to lead the science team.

targetWords.definition: To launch something means to make it go into motion.
targetWords.example: The boat launched from the dock and floated down the river.

targetWords.definition: If something is meteorological, it is concerned with the science of weather.
targetWords.example: The thunderstorm was so large that it became a great meteorological event.

targetWords.definition: Meteorology is the science that studies the weather.
targetWords.example: In order to understand the weather, you have to study meteorology.

targetWords.definition: To penetrate something means to enter into it.
targetWords.example: The knife easily penetrated the surface o f the orange.

targetWords.definition: Propulsion is the force that moves something forward.
targetWords.example: The propulsion lifted the rocket into the sky.

targetWords.definition: To simulate something means to copy its actions or characteristics.
targetWords.example: The French language teacher could simulate the accent o f a French citizen.

targetWords.definition: To spur someone means to urge them into action.
targetWords.example: The coach's speech spurred her team into playing the best game o f their lives.

targetWords.definition: To stimulate something means to cause or to increase activity in it.
targetWords.example: Doctors sometimes use electric shock to stimulate a patient's heartbeat.

targetWords.definition: If someone is tenacious, then they do not easily give up.
targetWords.example: I'm sure that he'll finish that difficult sale. He is very tenacious.

story.title: The Tenacious Inventor
story.passage:
A young student of meteorology was having a difficult time with an experiment. He was

attempting to duplicate lightning in clouds. He had made a device that could simulate

lightning. It worked by releasing an electromagnetic pulse into the cloud. This pulse,

in turn, stimulated the electrons in the cloud's particles. Then the electrons produced

lightning.

But his meteorological experiment had a major defect. He couldn't get the device into

the sky.

He had tied it to balloons, but they had burst. He had shot the device from a cannon, but

the force of the cannon had damaged it.

"You should give up," his friends told him. "You' ll never get that thing into the air."

But his friends' criticisms only spurred him to try again. The student was very innovative,

and at last, he thought that he had an innovation that would work. He attached wings to

the device, and on one dreary day, when clouds blocked the light of the sun, he started his

experiment anew.

He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky. The propulsion of the

rocket carried the device high into the air. The rocket accelerated into the clouds and then

released the device. It glided on its wings through the clouds, and when it penetrated

the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse. And just as he had

predicted, lightning shot from the cloud!

He called his professors, and the next day they came to watch. He successfully

duplicated the experiment. His teachers were extremely impressed and called the student

and his invention ingenious.

The student was given many awards and became a famous inventor. He had not given

up. He had remained tenacious and succeeded.

questions.question: The student of meteorology had bought a device that simulated lightning in clouds.
The electromagnetic pulse stimulated the electrons in the cloud's particles.
The student's friends' criticisms spurred him to try his experiment anew.
It was a dreary day when the device glided into the clouds.
The propulsion of the rocket accelerated the speed of the lightning.
What was the defect of the student's meteorological experiment?
What innovation did the innovative student use to launch his device into the clouds?
For whom did the student duplicate his ingenious experiment?
What did the device do when it finally penetrated the center of a large black cloud?
What happened to the student because he was tenacious?
